auditor: description: GUILD AUDITOR (opus tier) that holds the orchestrator's own work—the constitution and the task decomposition—to the same bar as workers. Dispatch via the guild lifecycle with an Audit-ID (CON-audit or DEC-audit).
tools: Read, Bash, Write, Grep, Glob
checker-courier: description: GUILD CHECKER (courier) that relays a judgment check to an external vendor CLI over a lane (codex today), producing a SECOND-OPINION verdict at a lane-suffixed stem. Dispatch only via the guild lifecycle with a Task-ID.
checker-deterministic: description: GUILD CHECKER (haiku tier) that runs a task's named check scripts and transcribes the results into a verdict, exercising zero judgment. For clauses whose check is a deterministic script. Dispatch only via the guild lifecycle with a Task-ID.
tools: Read, Bash, Write, Grep, Glob
checker-judgment: description: GUILD CHECKER (opus tier) that verifies taste and correctness clauses by re-deriving every claim from the artifacts, ignoring the worker's self-report. For clauses whose check is a judgment rubric. Dispatch only via the guild lifecycle with a Task-ID.
tools: Read, Bash, Write, Grep, Glob
hydrator: Runs the five-phase working-memory hydration pipeline — discover, extract, draft,
reconcile, propose — to surface candidate working-memory content from a project's
existing source artifacts for human review. Use when populating working memory
beyond the installer's pre-population (deeper one-time hydration).
worker-bulk: description: GUILD WORKER (haiku tier) for mechanical, zero-judgment execution—renames, moves, format conversions, boilerplate, exact-spec data entry. Dispatch only via the guild lifecycle with a Task-ID.
worker-craft: description: GUILD WORKER (opus tier) for user-facing, taste-sensitive work—copy, UI, visual design, anything a person reads or sees and judges on quality of craft. Dispatch only via the guild lifecycle with a Task-ID.
worker-standard: description: GUILD WORKER (sonnet tier) for clear-spec implementation—code, config, and structured content where the spec is explicit and the work is judged on correctness. Dispatch only via the guild lifecycle with a Task-ID.
working-memory-synchronizer: Synchronizes working memory with project state. Invoke after completing a feature,
making an architectural decision, or when activeContext.md feels stale.

audition: description: Run a candidate model through a fixed tryout battery before trusting it in the guild—scored, timed, logged. Use when evaluating a new or swapped model for a worker or checker tier, or deciding where a model belongs in the routing table.
constitution: description: Phase 0 of a guild job. Interview the user, then write .agent-guild/state/constitution.md—the falsifiable standard every task is checked against. Use when starting a job, defining what "done right" means, or writing or refreshing the constitution before decomposing work.
decompose: description: Phase 1 of a guild job. Turn .agent-guild/state/spec.md plus the constitution into task files under .agent-guild/state/tasks/, each with an executor, a checker, and a check method. Use after the constitution passes audit, when breaking a job into dispatchable work.
hydrate-discover: Inventory the source surface for hydrating working memory in this repo.
Surveys manifests, code structure, README, ADRs (if any), recent git history,
and code patterns. Run once when populating working memory beyond the
hydrate-draft: Map findings into the six working memory files: projectOverview, decisionLog,
dataContracts, conventions, openQuestions. Drafts include source provenance
inline. activeContext.md is excluded; the developer drives that file directly.
hydrate-extract: Pull findings from a single source location. Each finding is one sentence
about a fact, decision, convention, or contract, plus a pointer back to
source. Deterministic for structured sources, AI semantic for prose.
hydrate-propose: Stage reconciled drafts as a single commit (or PR for multi-developer projects)
that updates the working memory files in a reviewable batch. activeContext.md
is excluded. After acceptance, the synchronizer agent takes over for ongoing
hydrate-reconcile: Compare drafts against existing working memory and against the codebase.
Annotates each draft as net-new, would-overwrite, or conflicts-with-code.
Greenfield projects skip the existing-working-memory comparison.
init: description: Finishes a guild plugin install inside a project by copying the per-project payload (the orchestrator contract, check-script tooling, and templates) that a plugin can't ship as always-on config. Explicit-only — the model never invokes this on its own; the user runs it by name. Use when the user says "finish the guild install here" or "set up this project for the guild".
job: description: Phase 0 intake for a guild job. Turns an existing GitHub issue or a BYO spec ($ARGUMENTS — issue number, owner/repo#N, issue URL, local file path, or other URL) into .agent-guild/state/spec.md with a provenance header, then flows straight into /constitution. Use when starting a job from an issue or an existing document — "build issue #12", "kick off a job from this spec".
retrospective: description: Phase 3 of a guild job. Read the run state and write .agent-guild/state/retrospective.md—what the checkers caught, where retries and escalations clustered, how disputes were ruled. Use at the end of a job, or when reviewing how a build went and what the constitution missed.
update-working-memory: Reads the current working memory state, diffs it against recent git changes,
and proposes updates. Use when finishing a feature, resolving a decision,
or when active context feels stale.

agent_body_suffixes.checker-courier:
## Claude Host: Codex Lane

On a Claude host, the lane is `codex`, the far-side provider is `openai`, and the pinned model is `gpt-5.6-terra`. A Claude-hosted job must never call Claude for its own second opinion.

Compose the brief with that identity, so the far side is told the values the runner will record it against:

```sh
python3 .agent-guild/scripts/compose-brief.py <Task-ID> --vendor openai --model gpt-5.6-terra
```

Inline the `Task-ID`, complete brief, artifact contents or diff, and local evidence into one prompt file at an absolute scratch path. Writing that file is what your `Write` tool is for and the only thing it is for; the runner owns every other write. The far side receives no repository paths as substitutes for evidence, and has no tools or remote-command surface.

Invoke the fixed boundary with the complete prompt on stdin:

```sh
python3 .agent-guild/scripts/codex-courier.py --task-id <Task-ID> --tier <tier> --retries <retries> --brief .agent-guild/state/briefs/<Task-ID>.md < <ABSOLUTE prompt scratch path>
```

The runner pins the model with `-m gpt-5.6-terra` and `--ignore-user-config`, runs `codex exec` read-only and ephemeral from an isolated empty cwd with the child stdin closed, requires structured output against the canonical schema, enforces a wall-clock bound, and never reads the output file of a process it killed. It independently validates the verdict and verifies `task_id`, `checker`, and `vendor`. It does not ask the far side what model answered: it stamps the model the lane ran, records any divergence from what the vendor echoed as an `info` finding, and retains the raw response. A crossing is never discarded over that field. Malformed output is retried once; a structured quota status is classified before any wording fallback.

This host is writable, so the runner persists everything itself: the verdict at `.agent-guild/state/verdicts/<Task-ID>-<tier>-r<retries>-codex.json`, its rendered Markdown sibling, and exactly one `ledger-append.py` line with lane vendor `codex`. On a quota signal it appends the `--quota-event` line first, then creates `.agent-guild/state/exhausted/codex`, and writes no verdict. Do not repeat any of those writes by hand and never hand-format a ledger line. Run the script once and report the JSON it printed.

Missing CLI access, authentication failure, timeout, and twice-malformed output all arrive as a schema-conforming `blocked` suffixed verdict with its ledger line. None of them replaces or alters the unsuffixed in-family verdict of record.

## Claude Plugin Command

Run the shared installer from the installed plugin:

```sh
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/project-template/install.py" claude "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}"
```

After it succeeds, start existing work with `/agent-guild:job <issue|file|url>` or author a fresh spec with `/agent-guild:constitution`.
